reasoning: English loan, so p keeps its Latin letter; long aa then long oo. Far more common in Ramallah than 7aasuub ma7muul.
Emphatic ط and a long uu in the second syllable. Refers to the celebration as much as the act itself, as in 3azamna 3ala Tuhuur.
Palestinian has t here, not th, and two short a vowels. Used for sending messages, people or things.
Collective noun with a glottal ق; some Ramallah speakers round the second vowel to bundu'. A single nut is 7abbet bunda'.
Italian loan, long aa then a final o. Often used loosely for the bathroom itself as well as the tub.
Palestinian imperative 3aTiini, without the MSA hamza of a3Tini, and ق is a glottal stop. nimirtak is just as natural for the number.
Simple past he-form with two short a vowels. Takes a direct object: shakarni.
Two short a vowels, ع as 3. Used of planting a seedling and of putting land under crop.
The first vowel drops to an initial cluster in Palestinian. The zip sense is genuine and sits alongside the identical word for clouds; context separates them.
Emphatic ط twice and a glottal ق in ma'liyye. Covers both chips and crisps-style fried potato on a menu.
Country name beginning on a cluster sw-, with a long ii. Pronounced the same across the Levant.
Form III with a long aa, glottal ق and emphatic ط. The same verb means to boycott, which in Palestine is at least as frequent a sense.
ق is a glottal stop in ordinary speech, though news register keeps nafaq. Plural anfaa'.
Understood and used everywhere, including Ramallah, but the default local word for money is maSaari. Initial cluster fl- with a long uu.
hal- is the reduced haada il-, and ح stays a moon letter so no assimilation. 7aki is the Palestinian noun for talk.
The article assimilates to the sun letter ش, and ض is emphatic D. Said in Ramallah, though ish-shahr illi faat is the more colloquial turn.
Blessing form with no b- prefix and short i vowels. Also used as a politeness marker before mentioning something unclean.
baTn is feminine, so the b- present takes bit-, and the shadda doubles the ج. Emphatic ط in baTni.
Form X of a final weak root; the helping vowel at the start is usually dropped, giving the cluster st-. The children's game is ghummeeDa or staghmaaya.
b- present for the modal, bare subjunctive for the second verb, both with ق as a glottal stop. halla' is the Palestinian now, with a final glottal stop.
3a plus the article assimilates to the sun letter ش, giving 3ash-shajara, and taa marbuta after ر is a. wala here means rather than, the comparison the English spells out as better than.
Unit noun from the collective tiin, with a long ii and e after ن. It names the tree, like zaytuune, and also a single fig.
The first vowel drops, leaving the cluster dj-, and many Ramallah speakers simplify it further to jaaj. Collective, both the live birds and the meat.
Initial cluster ghr- with a long aa. Plural ghirbaan.
Two long aa vowels and the abstract ending -iyye with a doubled y. The written form is often raa'smaaliyye, but speech has no glottal stop there.
